articles.title: Netflix reajusta preços dos planos no Brasil; veja novos valores | G1
articles.standfirst: Reajuste chega um dia após notícia de que a empresa pretende cortar cerca de mil vagas; plano com anúncios tem maior alta percentual, de 23,9%.
articles.summary: Reajuste chega um dia após notícia de que a empresa pretende cortar cerca de mil vagas; plano com anúncios tem maior alta percentual, de 23,9%.
articles.body:
Netflix reajusta preços dos planos no Brasil; premium chega a R$ 71,90 — Foto: REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas

A Netflix aumentou nesta semana os preços dos três planos de assinatura no Brasil. Com a mudança, o plano mais caro, que permite assistir a conteúdos em até quatro telas simultâneas e oferece qualidade 4K+HDR, passa a custar R$ 71,90 por mês.

O reajuste ocorre em meio à notícia de que a Netflix pretende demitir cerca de mil funcionários, o equivalente a 6% de sua força de trabalho global . Essa será a maior rodada de cortes da plataforma de streaming desde 2022.

O maior aumento percentual foi no plano Padrão com anúncios, que ficou 23,9% mais caro. A modalidade permite assistir a conteúdos em até dois dispositivos simultaneamente, com qualidade Full HD.

Padrão com anúncios: de R$ 20,90 para R$ 25,90 (alta de 23,9%);

Padrão: de R$ 44,90 para R$ 51,90 (alta de 15,6%);

Premium: de R$ 59,90 para R$ 71,90 (alta de 20%).

Em resposta ao g1 , a empresa afirmou que busca entregar "mais valor" aos assinantes e por isso optou por atualizar os preços, "para continuar investindo em entretenimento de qualidade e melhorar a experiência de todos".

"Continuamos oferecendo filmes, séries, reality shows e muito mais – com opções para diferentes orçamentos", disse em nota.

O último reajuste da Netflix no Brasil havia ocorrido em maio de 2024, quando os preços dos planos subiram cerca de 12% . Na ocasião, a empresa afirmou que os aumentos permitiam ampliar a oferta de filmes e séries aos assinantes.

Nesta quarta-feira (14), o The Wall Street Journal noticiou os planos da Netflix de demitir cerca de mil funcionários, o equivalente a aproximadamente 6% de sua força de trabalho.

A decisão, segundo o jornal, foi comunicada por e-mail enviado pelos co-presidentes executivos da companhia, Greg Peters e Ted Sarandos.

A maior parte dos cortes deve atingir as equipes de produto, tecnologia, recursos humanos e o departamento jurídico.

No fim de 2025, a empresa tinha cerca de 16 mil funcionários em tempo integral. Procurada pela agência de notícias Reuters, a Netflix não respondeu imediatamente ao pedido de comentário.

📺 As demissões ocorrem em um cenário de concorrência crescente pela atenção dos consumidores e de mudanças no mercado global de entretenimento, marcado pela concentração de empresas e pela disputa por conteúdo e serviços de streaming.

Para diversificar as fontes de receita, a Netflix tem investido em publicidade, programação ao vivo e jogos, além do modelo tradicional de assinaturas.

A empresa busca ampliar as formas de monetização de sua base de usuários em um mercado no qual disputa espaço com plataformas digitais, emissoras e outros serviços de streaming.

Um dos movimentos recentes que ilustram a consolidação do setor foi a disputa pelos ativos de estúdio e streaming da Warner Bros. Discovery.

A Netflix participou da concorrência, mas perdeu para a Paramount Skydance, que concluiu neste mês a aquisição da companhia por US$ 110 bilhões .

A operação reúne sob o mesmo grupo importantes marcas do entretenimento e do jornalismo, como Warner Bros., Paramount Pictures, HBO Max, Paramount+, CNN e CBS.

O negócio também combina franquias cinematográficas como Harry Potter, Batman, Missão: Impossível e Top Gun, além de estúdios, plataformas de streaming e redes de televisão.

Com a fusão, a companhia combinada passa a concentrar operações em cinema, televisão, streaming e jornalismo.

O grupo terá cerca de US$ 80 bilhões em dívidas e será liderado por David Ellison. As ações passaram a ser negociadas na Bolsa de Nova York sob o código “SKYD”, após deixarem a Nasdaq.

A aquisição encerra uma das principais disputas recentes pelo controle de ativos de Hollywood e reforça a tendência de consolidação entre grandes empresas de mídia, que buscam reunir catálogos de conteúdo, canais de distribuição e diferentes fontes de receita para competir por audiência.

articles.title: Vigilância Sanitária descarta 60 kg de alimentos vencidos em Cabo Frio | G1
articles.standfirst: A ação ocorreu após uma denúncia divulgada pelo g1; A Fiscalização encontrou carnes fora da validade e outras irregularidades; estabelecimento foi advertido e passará por nova inspeção.
articles.summary: A ação ocorreu após uma denúncia divulgada pelo g1; A Fiscalização encontrou carnes fora da validade e outras irregularidades; estabelecimento foi advertido
articles.body:
Também foram apreendidos e descartados produtos com prazo de validade vencido, totalizando 60 quilos de alimentos. — Foto: Vigilância Sanitária de Cabo Frio

A Vigilância Sanitária da Secretaria de Saúde de Cabo Frio , na Região dos Lagos do Rio, descartou 60 quilos de alimentos fora da validade durante uma fiscalização realizada nesta quinta-feira (15) em um supermercado no bairro Jardim Esperança.

A ação ocorreu após uma denúncia divulgada pelo g1 , na qual um cliente filmou uma barata andando sobre produtos expostos . Durante a inspeção, porém, os fiscais não constataram a presença de insetos no estabelecimento.

O supermercado foi advertido e deverá passar por uma nova fiscalização nos próximos dias.

De acordo com a superintendente da Vigilância Sanitária, Kelly de Araújo, o estabelecimento já foi fiscalizado diversas vezes ao longo deste ano.

Durante a inspeção, os fiscais encontraram excesso de pallets de madeira e papelões no salão de vendas, e determinaram a retirada desses materiais.

Também foram apreendidos e descartados produtos com prazo de validade vencido, totalizando 60 quilos de alimentos. Entre os itens inutilizados estavam 44 quilos de pernil e 15 quilos de costela suína.

Além da advertência, a Vigilância Sanitária determinou uma série de adequações ao supermercado, incluindo a redução do intervalo entre as dedetizações, de 15 para 10 dias, a reavaliação da validade dos produtos expostos e a diminuição do intervalo de limpeza do salão.

Os fiscais também solicitaram a troca ou o reparo das tampas dos expositores de frangos congelados, já que, quando permanecem abertas, podem atrair vetores.

Denúncias à Vigilância Sanitária podem ser encaminhadas para o e-mail vigilancia.sanitaria@gmail.com.

articles.title: Apostas ilegais no RN: investigados pagarão R$ 1,4 milhão | G1
articles.standfirst: Acordo prevê pagamento de R$ 200 mil e perda de outros R$ 1,2 milhão para os cofres estaduais; investigação da Operação Conto da Sorte continua.
articles.summary: O acordo da Operação Conto da Sorte envolve a devolução de lucros e multas após investigações sobre o uso da Lotseridó e sites oficiais para promover apostas ilegais no RN.
articles.body:
Acordo de Não Persecução Penal foi firmado com o MPRN — Foto: MPRN/Divulgação

Três pessoas investigadas por envolvimento em um esquema de apostas ilegais confessaram práticas ilícitas e firmaram um acordo com o Ministério Público do Rio Grande do Norte (MPRN). O acordo, segundo o órgão, prevê o pagamento de R$ 200 mil e a perda de outros R$ 1,2 milhão, totalizando R$ 1,4 milhão.

O caso faz parte da Operação Conto da Sorte, que investiga um grupo suspeito de explorar jogos de azar usando, entre outros recursos, a Lotseridó, loteria criada pela Prefeitura de Bodó , no interior do Rio Grande do Norte.

As investigações também apontaram o uso de empresas de fachada e de sistemas digitais para direcionar usuários a sites de apostas ilegais. As apurações continuam em relação aos demais investigados.

O g1 buscou posicionamento da Prefeitura de Bodó, mas não houve resposta até a última atualização desta matéria.

Pelo acordo de não persecução penal (ANPP), os três envolvidos pagarão os R$ 200 mil de forma parcelada. O valor será dividido entre a Receita Federal e o Ministério da Fazenda. Já os R$ 1,2 milhão correspondem à perda definitiva de recursos apontados como lucro presumido do esquema, que serão destinados aos cofres estaduais.

O acordo também estabelece que empresas ligadas ao grupo comprovem a implantação de um programa de integridade, conhecido como compliance, no prazo de 180 dias.

Segundo as investigações do MPRN, o grupo usava a Lotseridó, loteria criada pela Prefeitura de Bodó, no interior do Rio Grande do Norte, como parte da estrutura investigada. O caso envolve suspeitas de exploração de jogos sem autorização e ocultação de recursos.

Outra frente investigada envolve a inserção de códigos em páginas de órgãos públicos e instituições de ensino, inclusive em sites com domínio “.gov.br” e “.edu.br”. A prática teria criado arquivos que direcionavam mecanismos de busca e usuários para páginas de apostas ilegais, dando aparência de credibilidade aos sites.

O grupo também teria usado empresas registradas em nome de terceiros para movimentar recursos. De acordo com o MPRN, algumas empresas funcionavam em endereços inexistentes, salas comerciais vazias ou escritórios virtuais.

Em Bodó, os investigadores identificaram 21 empresas registradas em um mesmo endereço apontado como fictício.

A Operação Conto da Sorte teve ações em Pernambuco, São Paulo e Ceará, além da investigação conduzida no Rio Grande do Norte.

O trabalho começou após uma análise técnica da Secretaria de Prêmios e Apostas do Ministério da Fazenda e contou com a participação de órgãos federais e Ministérios Públicos de outros estados.

Entre os crimes investigados estão lavagem de dinheiro, exploração de jogos de azar, operação de loteria sem autorização, associação criminosa e delitos contra as relações de consumo.

articles.title: Washington pastor Cristian Popescu accused of $13 million investment fraud targeting over 30 investors; allegedly told church members God chose them to invest and called critics demonically possessed
articles.summary: A Washington pastor has been indicted on federal charges of wire fraud and money laundering over an alleged $13 million investment scheme that prosecutors
articles.body: A Washington pastor has been indicted on federal charges of wire fraud and money laundering over an alleged $13 million investment scheme that prosecutors say targeted members of his own congregation. Cristian Popescu, 46, pastor of Passion for Christ, a Christian congregation in Kirkland, Washington, allegedly persuaded more than 30 investors to invest in a company he claimed was a successful online marketplace preparing for a stock market listing.According to a press release issued by the US Department of Justice (DOJ), Popescu pleaded not guilty when he appeared in US District Court in Seattle. He faces 10 counts of wire fraud and five counts of money laundering. His trial is scheduled for December 21, 2026. He has been released under electronic monitoring while awaiting trial, despite prosecutors’ objections.The indictment alleges that Popescu used his position as a pastor to gain investors’ trust and misrepresented the financial health and prospects of Followone Inc., a Bellevue-based company he claimed to operate.Pastor allegedly used faith to attract investorsAccording to the DOJ, Popescu began promoting Followone as early as 2015, presenting it as a global online marketplace and social networking platform through which users could buy and sell products and services, including cars, real estate, healthcare, food and travel.Prosecutors allege that the platform was largely non-functional and that Popescu misled investors about its operations, revenue and valuation. He allegedly claimed the company was generating millions of dollars, that investments were appreciating and that Followone was approaching a Nasdaq listing.The indictment further alleges that Popescu used his religious standing to convince members of his congregation to invest. He reportedly told them that God had chosen them for the opportunity and that their investments would support the church’s mission. He also allegedly assured investors that their money would remain in the company and could be withdrawn at any time.Acting US Attorney Charles Neil Floyd said the defendant allegedly created the appearance of a valuable online marketplace before using investors’ money for personal benefit.“As alleged in the indictment, this defendant created the mirage of a successful, valuable online marketplace and social media site in one,” Floyd said, according to the DOJ statement.Company allegedly valued at $1.4 billion despite having little valueProsecutors allege that Popescu used misleading press releases, websites and expensive office space to make Followone appear to be a thriving business. He allegedly claimed that the company had recruited top software engineers and employed 20 people, although the indictment says only three people worked there.Popescu also allegedly maintained a website that showed purported growth in investors’ holdings and claimed Followone was worth $1.4 billion, despite allegedly knowing that the business had little or no value.The company rented expensive offices in Bellevue to reinforce its image, according to prosecutors. It was eventually evicted after allegedly accumulating more than $350,000 in unpaid rent.Investors allegedly urged to withdraw savings and take loansThe DOJ said Popescu allegedly encouraged investors to commit substantial sums to Followone, telling them they could secure positions on the company’s board if they invested $1 million.According to the indictment, he urged some investors to access retirement accounts, take out personal or home equity loans, and use money saved for their children’s college education.Prosecutors also allege that Popescu imposed strict communication requirements. Investors were reportedly asked to sign non-disclosure agreements and use encrypted messaging services. During meetings, he allegedly instructed them to switch off their phones and other smart devices.When investors later asked for their money back, Popescu allegedly delayed repayment, claiming that returning funds could jeopardise the planned stock market listing. He also allegedly invoked his religious position when challenged and told some investors they were demonically possessed.FBI Seattle Special Agent in Charge W. Mike Herrington said the charges allege that Popescu exploited the trust of fellow believers through promises of a future stock market listing and claims that the profits would benefit the community.More than $4.5 million allegedly transferred to family accountsAccording to the indictment, more than $4.5 million in Followone funds was allegedly transferred to accounts belonging to Popescu, his wife and other family members.Prosecutors further allege that Popescu paid himself more than $1 million in wages from the company between 2017 and 2024. His wife, who allegedly was not employed by Followone, received approximately $300,000.The wire fraud charges relate to alleged investment solicitations and payments, while the money laundering counts concern alleged transfers from Followone accounts to Popescu’s personal account. The indictment cites individual investments that included nearly $1 million in one transaction, as well as other sums of approximately $600,000 and $500,000.IRS Criminal Investigation Seattle Field Office Special Agent in Charge Carrie Nordyke said financial crimes can cause significant harm to victims, particularly when offenders allegedly abuse positions of trust.Trial scheduled for December 2026The case is being investigated by the FBI and the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation division. Assistant US Attorney Seth Wilkinson is prosecuting the case.Wire fraud carries a maximum statutory penalty of 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine. Money laundering carries a maximum statutory penalty of 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine. The maximum penalties do not indicate what sentence, if any, would be imposed.Popescu has pleaded not guilty and is scheduled to stand trial on December 21, 2026. The DOJ has clarified that the indictment contains allegations and that the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pilot reports wing icing before plane crashes in Wisconsin; 6 killed
articles.summary: An experienced pilot and five other people were killed when a six-seat plane crashed in a wooded area near Mirror Lake State Park in Wisconsin, US, on
articles.body: An experienced pilot and five other people were killed when a six-seat plane crashed in a wooded area near Mirror Lake State Park in Wisconsin, US, on Tuesday night, after the pilot reported ice building up on its wings during a thunderstorm. The Piper PA-46 Malibu was flying from Kenosha to Menomonie when it lost contact with air traffic control shortly before 10pm.The pilot, identified as longtime aviator Ron Riek, was also a prominent local warehouse owner. Authorities have not yet released the names of the five other victims. No one on the ground was injured.According to the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), the pilot reported icing on the wings while flying at 24,000 feet (7,315 metres) and requested permission to descend. Air traffic control approved the request.The plane then began a right-hand descending turn. The rate of descent increased sharply before communications and tracking data were lost. The aircraft crashed near the popular tourist destination of Wisconsin Dells.Ice accumulation is a serious aviation hazard. Even a thin layer can disrupt airflow over a plane's wings and make it difficult to remain airborne.Experienced pilot remembered as 'a good man'Menomonie Airport Commission chairman Daniel Johnson confirmed Riek's death at a public meeting on Wednesday night. He described the pilot, whom he had known for decades, as an experienced aviator and a close friend.“He was simply a good man. A highly experienced pilot, and this was simply a tragedy,” Johnson said.Federal Aviation Administration records show that Riek held an airline transport pilot rating. This indicates that he had at least 1,500 hours of flying experience and met the requirements for the highest level of pilot certification used by airlines.The NTSB is leading the investigation into the crash. Investigators are expected to examine the aircraft's history and previous crashes involving the Piper PA-46 Malibu, including incidents linked to icing.The agency conducted a safety study of seven crashes involving Piper aircraft between 1989 and 1991.Johnson said “the aircraft has a reputation of not doing well in thunderstorms.”Second fatal plane crash in 18 monthsThe latest crash has shaken the aviation community around Menomonie, which suffered another fatal accident last year. Four people died in that crash.Riek had helped organise a fundraiser after the earlier accident to support the three young children of a couple who were killed."This is two fatal crashes in 18 months. We’ve lost a lot of friends,” Johnson said. “This creates a hole in the aviation community.”The crash occurred near Wisconsin Dells, a major tourist destination known for its concentration of waterparks. The area markets itself as the “Waterpark Capital of the World” and attracted more than five million visitors in 2025, according to state tourism officials.You use AI every day. articles.title: Two Indiana teen brothers, 15 and 14, jumped into a retention pond to save a grandmother and two young children; one pulled a submerged 2-year-old from a stroller and got the toddler breathing again
articles.summary: Two teenage brothers jumped into a murky pond in Carmel, Indiana, to rescue a grandmother, her four-year-old grandchild, and a toddler trapped underwater
articles.body: Two teenage brothers jumped into a murky pond in Carmel, Indiana, to rescue a grandmother, her four-year-old grandchild, and a toddler trapped underwater in a pushchair. Maddox Larger, 15, and his 14-year-old brother, Grant, jumped into the water on Monday, 12 October 2026, after seeing the family in danger. Their quick actions helped save a two-year-old boy who had stopped breathing underwater. One of the teenagers performed emergency back slaps on dry land to help the child breathe again. According to an official statement from the City of Carmel, local police and fire crews were called to the scene at around 11:15 a.m. after emergency calls reported children underwater.A sudden struggle in deep waterThe emergency began when the grandmother was walking near the pond with her two young grandchildren. The pushchair carrying the two-year-old slipped into the water and became partly submerged. As the grandmother tried to pull the pushchair out, she lost her footing and fell into the pond. She had the four-year-old child strapped to her back. Neither the grandmother nor the older child knew how to swim, leaving them struggling in the water with little chance of getting out on their own. When Maddox and Grant Larger saw what was happening nearby, they ran to the pond and jumped straight into the water to help. The brothers reached the grandmother first. They supported her and helped guide her and the four-year-old child safely back to the shore.Performing life-saving first aidOnce the grandmother and four-year-old were safely on dry land, Maddox turned his attention to the pushchair still submerged in the pond. He pulled the heavy, water-soaked pushchair out of the water and quickly unbuckled the trapped two-year-old. The toddler was unresponsive and not breathing, so Maddox immediately began giving back slaps to help clear the child's airway. His quick action worked. The treatment helped force water out of the toddler's lungs. Soon, the child began breathing again and started to cry. By the time crews from the Carmel Fire Department and Carmel Police Department arrived, both children were safely out of the water. First responders checked the two-year-old and four-year-old at the scene. They confirmed that both children were conscious, crying, and in stable condition.Praise from local authoritiesPublic safety officials in Carmel praised the teenagers for acting quickly and helping prevent a tragedy. "The immediate actions taken by Maddox and Grant demonstrated remarkable courage and quick thinking under pressure," said Sgt. Matt Keinsley of the Carmel Police Department in an official media release. "Their heroic efforts made the difference between a tragedy and a miraculous outcome." City officials also pointed out that the pond was dangerous because of its steep sides and murky water. These conditions made it difficult to see what was happening underwater and meant that quick action was vital.Civic recognition planned at city councilThe rescue has earned widespread praise across the suburban Indianapolis community. To recognise their bravery and quick response in a dangerous situation, city leaders confirmed that Maddox and Grant Larger will receive formal honours at an upcoming public ceremony. According to official event details published by the City of Carmel, the brothers will receive commendations for their life-saving actions during the Carmel City Council meeting scheduled for 16 November 2026.You use AI every day. articles.title: Yemen says 1,250 strikes rained on Houthis within 24 hours, claims over 700 Houthis killed
articles.summary: Yemen armed forces on Thursday claimed they conducted 1,250 targeting operations against the Houthis within the past 24 Hours, as the Iran-backed group
articles.body: Yemen armed forces on Thursday claimed they conducted 1,250 targeting operations against the Houthis within the past 24 Hours, as the Iran-backed group targeted Aden’s presidential palace and launched several strikes over Saudi regions.Armed forces spokesperson colonel Majed Al-Nuzaili said the strikes were carried out under the recently launched Operation "Dawn of Yemen".He said the armed forces conducted “more than (1250) precise targeting operations over the past 24 hours, against sites and military capabilities belonging to the terrorist Houthi militia, using warplanes, drones, field artillery, rocket launchers, and sniper units.”The spokesperson claimed nearly 700 “militia elements” were neutralised in the attacks.“Initial field estimates indicate the neutralisation of approximately (700) militia elements, and the destruction or disabling of more than (150) vehicles, cars, combat, transport, and supply means,” Nuzaili said in an X post.He added that the targeting focused on frontline defence networks, fortifications and trenches, sources of fire, observation and reconnaissance points, advanced command and control sites, areas of troop concentration and reserve deployment, and transportation and supply means.Yemen forces claimed the operations achieved direct results, including the dismantling of Houthi’s defensive networks, the destruction of its formations and offensive capabilities, and the obliteration of its fortifications, trenches, and combat positions.“Particularly on the Taiz fronts, where our forces continue to bleed the militia and break its assaults,” Nuzaili saidAdditionally, the forces said strikes were carried out in accordance with the rules of international humanitarian law, where the army took necessary precautions to protect civilians and civilian assets.Houthi share of attacksThe Houthi rebels, on the other hand, targeted Yemen's Al-Maashiq presidential palace in Aden through strikes that killed at least four and wounded several others.Yemen’s minister of youth Nayef Saleh al-Bakri said no minister present in the palace was harmed, asking the members to not leave the city following the incident. Al Arabiya reported.Hostilities have escalated between the Houthi movement and Saudi Arabia over the past two months, with the Yemeni group claiming to have carried out strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure and an international airport a day earlier.Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted two ballistic missiles directed towards Khamis Mushait in southwestern Saudi Arabia and neutralised three unmanned aerial vehicles north of Riyadh.Additionally, Saudis claimed a missile heading towards the Medina region was intercepted and destroyed. articles.title: In 2024, Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes put their game-worn Chiefs jerseys into a Kansas City charity auction; the NFL package sold for $250,000 as Big Slick raised $3.97 million for pediatric cancer
articles.summary: Two signed, game-worn jerseys donated by Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce sold for $250,000 at a charity auction in Missouri.
articles.body: Two signed, game-worn jerseys donated by Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce sold for $250,000 at a charity auction in Missouri. The sale helped raise millions of pounds for childhood cancer treatment. The NFL memorabilia package was one of the top items at the 15th annual Big Slick Celebrity Weekend in Kansas City. The two-day fundraising event brought together Hollywood actors, professional athletes, and thousands of supporters to raise money for the Cancer Center at Children's Mercy Hospital. Organisers confirmed at the end of the event that the weekend raised a record $3.97 million (£3.1 million) for childhood cancer research and patient care.Star power drives record biddingThe charity package included authentic game-worn jerseys signed by quarterback Patrick Mahomes and tight end Travis Kelce after their victory in Super Bowl LVIII. During the live auction at the T-Mobile Center, bidding quickly climbed past $100,000. The final winning bid reached $250,000 after Mahomes, Kelce, and celebrity hosts appeared on stage and encouraged the crowd to support the cause. The auction also offered special experiences alongside physical items. Other expensive lots included chances to appear in television productions, private meals with celebrity hosts, and VIP passes to major sporting events. According to event coverage published by the Kansas City Star, the annual charity weekend raised its highest total in a single year since it began. The $3.97 million total beat the previous record of $3.5 million, set in 2023.Hometown celebrities rally for local hospitalThe Big Slick event began in 2010 as a poker tournament organised by five actors who grew up in the Kansas City area. The original co-hosts were Paul Rudd, Jason Sudeikis, Rob Riggle, Eric Stonestreet, and David Koechner. Actor Heidi Gardner, who grew up in Kansas City and was formerly a cast member on Saturday Night Live, officially joined the group as a main co-host in 2023. Over the past decade, the organisers have turned the event from a small poker night into a large weekend gathering. The programme now includes a celebrity softball game at Kauffman Stadium, a bowling tournament, and a live entertainment show at the T-Mobile Center. Speaking to supporters during the event, co-host Rob Riggle reflected on how much the fundraiser had grown over its 15 years. "When we started this 15 years ago, we just wanted to raise a little money and bring some attention to the hospital," Riggle said during media appearances covered by local news outlets. "We never imagined it would grow into something this big."Supporting pediatric oncology researchAll money raised during the weekend goes directly to the Cancer Center at Children's Mercy Kansas City, one of the leading children's medical networks in the American Midwest. In an official public statement posted on LinkedIn after the event, representatives from Children's Mercy Hospital explained how important the annual donations are. The funds help pay for clinical trials, advanced diagnostic equipment, and support for families facing long treatment periods. "Big Slick is about our patients," the hospital stated in its online update. "Every dollar raised stays right here in Kansas City to support the kids and families fighting cancer at Children's Mercy." The hospital also noted that private donations from Big Slick help medical teams hire specialist doctors who treat childhood cancer. The money also helps expand access to experimental targeted treatments that traditional health insurance may not fully cover. Including the 2024 total, the Big Slick Celebrity Weekend has raised more than $21 million for Children's Mercy Hospital since the event began in 2010.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 1980, John Lennon and Yoko Ono bought a Palm Beach mansion for $725,000; after his death, Ono completed the renovation and sold it for $3.15 million, and the estate later sold again for $36 million
articles.summary: In January 1980, John Lennon and Yoko Ono purchased El Solano, a historic oceanfront mansion on Palm Beach’s South Ocean Boulevard, for $725,000.
articles.body: In January 1980, John Lennon and Yoko Ono purchased El Solano, a historic oceanfront mansion on Palm Beach’s South Ocean Boulevard, for $725,000. Lennon was killed in New York later that year, before the couple could complete the renovations they had planned for the Florida estate. Architectural Digest reports that Ono later finished the work and sold the home in 1986 for $3.15 million, while the property eventually sold again for $36 million.The mansion’s journey from a $725,000 purchase to a $36 million sale reflects both Palm Beach’s transformation into one of America’s most expensive housing markets and the lasting cultural interest in Lennon’s life. Known as El Solano, the estate remains one of the most notable celebrity-linked homes on Florida’s Billionaires Row.A historic mizner-designed estateEl Solano was built in 1919 by architect Addison Mizner, whose Mediterranean Revival work helped define Palm Beach’s early luxury architecture. The home features a stucco facade, terra-cotta roofing, and a grand, old-world style that still stands out along the waterfront.The estate spans roughly 1.3 acres and includes a three-car garage, two swimming pools, tennis courts, direct beach access, and a cabana. Architectural Digest describes the interior as lavish, with intricately designed ceilings, chandeliers, and French doors in the formal dining room that open toward the pool and ocean.The property is located at 720 South Ocean Boulevard, an address associated with Palm Beach’s most exclusive waterfront homes. Its neighbours have included musician Rod Stewart and author James Patterson, whose guest apartment shares a wall with the estate.Lennon and Ono bought without seeing itLennon and Ono bought the mansion in 1980, shortly before Lennon’s death in December of that year. According to Architectural Digest, the couple reportedly never set foot inside the seven-bedroom home before completing the purchase. Instead, they arranged for others to photograph the property so they could keep their identities hidden during the buying process. The approach reflected the intense public attention surrounding Lennon and Ono, even as they sought a private retreat far from New York.The couple planned extensive renovations after acquiring the estate. Those plans were interrupted when Lennon was fatally shot outside his residence in New York City later in 1980.Ono completed the renovationAfter Lennon’s death, Ono returned to Palm Beach and carried out the planned renovation work. Her involvement helped preserve and update the historic estate before she decided to sell it. In 1986, Ono sold El Solano for $3.15 million to New England developer Howard Fafard, as per reports. That sale represented a significant increase from the $725,000 the couple had paid six years earlier.The renovation and sale marked the end of the couple’s direct ownership, but it did not end the property’s connection to Lennon’s story. The mansion continued to be known as the former home of the Beatles legend and Ono, giving it a cultural value beyond its architecture and location.From $3.15 million to $23 millionEl Solano changed hands several times after Ono’s sale. In 1990, the estate sold for $4.31 million, showing how quickly its value continued to rise in Palm Beach’s growing luxury market, as per Deseret News.By 2016, the property sold for $23 million to John C. Sites Jr. and Cindy Sites, as per reports. The sale came three decades after Ono had sold the home for $3.15 million, illustrating the dramatic appreciation of prime Palm Beach real estate.The 2016 transaction also confirmed the estate’s status as a landmark property. Its oceanfront location, historic Mizner design, and celebrity provenance made it appealing to buyers seeking both privacy and prestige.The $36 million saleIn 2020, El Solano was listed for $47.5 million. Although the asking price was far higher than its eventual sale price, the estate ultimately sold for $36 million, according to Architectural Digest and reports citing The Wall Street Journal.The buyer was reported to be a young family relocating from the northeastern United States. The sale showed that even a substantial discount from the initial asking price did not diminish the property’s standing in Palm Beach’s ultra-luxury market.The $36 million sale was more than ten times Ono’s 1986 sale price and nearly 50 times the amount Lennon and Ono paid in 1980. It also confirmed El Solano’s place among Palm Beach’s most valuable historic homes.Why the estate remains significantEl Solano is significant because it combines three powerful elements: a historic Addison Mizner design, an oceanfront Palm Beach location, and a direct connection to John Lennon and Yoko Ono. Each factor has helped sustain interest in the property across generations.The estate also tells a story about how celebrity homes can become part of cultural history. Lennon and Ono owned the mansion for only a short period, yet their association with it has remained central to its identity long after the sale.For Palm Beach, the property represents the broader rise of Billionaires Row, where historic estates have become some of the most expensive homes in the United States. For music fans, it remains a rare physical link to Lennon’s final year and the life he shared with Ono.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: In 2011, Taylor Swift donated 6,000 books worth $68,000 to a Pennsylvania library that was struggling to stay open; 15 years later, it circulated 182,228 items and drew 27,452 program participants in 2025
articles.summary: When financial problems threatened to close public library branches across Berks County, Pennsylvania, a major donation from local native Taylor Swift
articles.body: When financial problems threatened to close public library branches across Berks County, Pennsylvania, a major donation from local native Taylor Swift helped keep them open for thousands of readers. In October 2011, the country music star donated 6,000 new books worth $68,000 (£52,000) to the Reading Public Library system. Fifteen years later, figures from the library network's official reports show that the system has grown into an important community resource. In 2025, it circulated 182,228 items and welcomed 27,452 people to its programs. Swift's donation came at a critical time, when cuts to local government budgets were putting heavy pressure on library services.Rescuing branch services in Berks CountySwift grew up nearby in Wyomissing, Pennsylvania. She learned about the Reading Public Library's money problems through local news reports and decided to help. According to reporting published by regional news outlet WHYY at the time, Swift bought thousands of popular books to refill empty shelves across all four city branches. Each donated book received a gold star on its spine and a special bookplate inside the front cover recognising the pop star's gift. The donation was shared equally among the main downtown library and three neighbourhood branches. This allowed readers across the wider Berks County library network to borrow the books. The arrival of many popular children's books, young adult novels, and general fiction helped library managers keep borrowing services running while local officials dealt with tight budgets.Expanding access and community engagementIn the years after Swift's widely reported donation, the Reading Public Library expanded its services beyond lending books. It became an important place for residents to learn, find information, and connect with others. Figures published in the Reading Public Library's 2025 Annual Appeal report show the scale of its work today across four branches. In addition to lending more than 182,000 physical and digital items in 2025, the system recorded 77,812 public computer sessions lasting 30 minutes each. These sessions gave job seekers, students, and local families important access to the internet. The library also expanded its learning programs for people of all ages. In 2025, a total of 27,452 people attended its general programs. Another 3,207 young children took part in early childhood reading programs. Activities include storytimes for young children, after-school sessions for teenagers, and digital skills classes. These classes help older adults and people looking for work learn how to use modern technology.Serving local patrons through targeted programsThe library system depends on a mix of local government funding and private donations to keep its services running. According to information in the library's official 2025 Annual Appeal documents, staff members provide personal help to people in need every day. Examples highlighted by the library include one-on-one digital skills lessons for adults changing careers, help with mobile phone enrolment for older people on low incomes, and home book delivery for residents living in assisted care facilities. The library's official mission statement describes it as a welcoming place that supports the community through free access to information, help finding reliable resources, and opportunities to keep learning throughout life. The main downtown branch at 100 South Fifth Street continues to serve local residents. It is also the main centre for public library services across Berks County. Fifteen years after thousands of donated books arrived with gold stars on their spines, the library system continues to build on that support. It remains an important centre for reading, learning, and public education across central Pennsylvania.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Cuban-American family claimed Cuba seized its island in 1959, won a $119.4 million verdict against Expedia companies, then saw a judge overturn it
articles.summary: The dispute over a Cuban island seized after the 1959 revolution has reached an unusual point in American legal history.
articles.body: The dispute over a Cuban island seized after the 1959 revolution has reached an unusual point in American legal history. As reported by Transnational Litigation Blog (TLB), in April 2025, a jury in Florida found four corporate defendants associated with Expedia liable under a US law dealing with property confiscated by the Cuban government. The award, reported at approximately $29.8 million per defendant, totaling $119.4 million, centred on a claim brought by Cuban-American businessman Mario Echevarría, whose family said it had lost its ownership rights to the island more than six decades earlier.A property dispute rooted in Cuba's revolutionary pastThe Cuban Revolution brought sweeping changes to property ownership, with the government confiscating assets claimed by private owners. Some former owners and their descendants later pursued claims in US courts under Title III of the Helms-Burton Act, enacted in 1996. The provision was activated for private lawsuits in 2019, allowing eligible claimants to seek damages over commercial activity involving property allegedly confiscated by Cuba.Echevarría maintained that his family had owned an island off Cuba's coast before the government took control of it. The property later became associated with tourism, with hotels operating on land that he alleged had been confiscated. His case was not simply about whether the family had once owned the island. It also asked whether companies facilitating hotel reservations could be held responsible for making money from property that had allegedly been taken unlawfully.The US law that reopened old confiscation claimsCongress passed the Cuban Liberty and Democratic Solidarity Act in 1996 (Helms-Burton Act). Its Title III provision created a route for eligible US nationals to seek compensation from people or companies that traffic in property confiscated by the Cuban government.For years, however, presidents suspended the provision allowing private lawsuits. That changed in 2019, when President Donald Trump ended the suspension, opening the door to claims that had previously been difficult or impossible to pursue under Title III.Why Expedia and its associated companies faced trialEchevarría brought his case against four corporate defendants associated with Expedia. Their involvement in online travel services placed them within the chain of commercial activity connected to the hotels, although their individual roles were not identical.Before trial, the defendants sought summary judgment on several grounds. They challenged Echevarría's claim to the property, disputed whether the land had been confiscated in a way that supported the lawsuit and argued that their booking services did not amount to trafficking. They also contested the extent to which damages could account for the hotels and other improvements rather than the underlying land alone.A further issue concerned the distinction between Expedia Group, Inc., the parent company, and the operating businesses that provided travel services. The parent company argued that it should not automatically be held responsible for the actions of its subsidiaries.In an opinion denying summary judgment, District Judge Federico Moreno concluded that important factual disputes remained unresolved. Questions about the family's ownership, the property's legal status under Cuban law and the relationship between the corporate entities could not simply be settled at that stage.The court also considered allegations that Expedia Group had signed lodging contracts with hotels and worked with Cuba's Ministry of Tourism to promote travel. Those activities raised questions about whether the parent company might have been directly involved in the relevant commercial arrangements, or whether the relationship between the businesses could support liability through an agency theory.What the $29.8 million verdict establishedIn April 2025, the jury found in Echevarría's favour against the four corporate defendants. The verdict was widely described as the first successful jury verdict under Title III of the Helms-Burton Act, giving the case significance beyond the immediate dispute over the island.The result indicated that the jury accepted the plaintiff's case sufficiently to find the defendants liable under the statute. The pre-trial ruling had identified several disputed questions, including whether the companies knowingly benefited from activity involving confiscated property and whether their conduct continued after they became aware of the lawsuit.However, the verdict should not be taken to mean that every legal argument raised before trial was resolved in the same way. The earlier ruling identified alternative routes to liability and factual questions for the jury. The reported award of approximately $29.8 million also illustrates the potential financial exposure associated with Title III claims.The questions that remain after the jury's decisionA verdict does not necessarily bring every dispute to an end. The legal consequences of the ruling depend on the subsequent procedural history, including any post-trial motions, challenges to the judgment or appeal. The April 2025 decision established a significant result for Echevarría, but it should not be treated as proof that every possible avenue of challenge has been exhausted.The underlying ownership questions also help explain why these cases can be difficult to resolve. The property was allegedly taken more than 60 years before the jury considered the dispute. Establishing who owned it at the time, how ownership passed through inheritance and what legal effect the confiscation had requires evidence and an examination of Cuban law.The evidence that led a judge to overturn the Expedia Cuba verdictAs reported by Miami Herald, the case took a decisive turn in September 2025, when a federal judge set aside the jury's verdict against Expedia-related companies. Judge Federico A. Moreno ruled that Echevarría had not provided sufficient evidence to establish that Expedia Group directly facilitated hotel bookings through its subsidiary, Expedia Inc. He also found that Orbitz and Hotels.com had not knowingly and intentionally trafficked in the confiscated property as required under the Helms-Burton Act. The original verdicts would have totalled approximately $119.4 million across four corporate defendants.Expedia Group welcomed the decision, saying the judge had found that the company did not violate the law. However, Echevarría's legal team indicated that it intended to continue fighting the case. The ruling marked a setback for the Cuban-American businessman, but it also highlighted the legal hurdles involved in proving that travel companies knowingly profited from property confiscated by the Cuban government. The outcome left the landmark case as a reminder that winning a jury verdict does not necessarily mean a claimant will ultimately secure damages.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: ED files PMLA case against FIITJEE and directors over alleged ₹85.79 crore student fee diversion; seeks confiscation of ₹71.88 crore in attached assets.
articles.body: Lucknow: Enforcement Directorate has filed a prosecution complaint against coaching institute FIITJEE Ltd and its directors, Dinesh Kumar Goel and Monila Goel, before a special PMLA court in Ghaziabad, alleging large-scale diversion and misappropriation of student fees collected for competitive exam coaching.The agency has sought their conviction under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act and confiscation of assets worth ₹71.88 crore that were seized or provisionally attached during the probe.Filed by the ED’s Lucknow Zonal Office on Oct 15, the complaint arises from an investigation into alleged siphoning of advance fees paid by students enrolled in FIITJEE’s programmes for engineering entrance examinations, including JEE.The ED said FIITJEE shut down 32 centres across the country between May 2024 and Feb 2025, leaving 14,411 students without services for which fees had already been paid.The agency has quantified the allegedly retained and misappropriated amount at ₹85.79 crore and termed it “proceeds of crime”.The money-laundering case stems from four FIRs registered in Noida, Greater Noida and Bhopal on allegations of cheating, criminal breach of trust and conspiracy. Investigators alleged the institute collected advance fees of ₹2.8 lakh to ₹3.5 lakh per student for courses spanning two to four years, while assuring uninterrupted coaching for the full programme period.Complaints alleged faculty began leaving after salaries were not paid, triggering operational disruption and closure of centres without prior notice.The ED further alleged FIITJEE continued enrolling students and collecting fees for programmes extending up to March 2029 despite being aware it could not deliver the promised services, and that it continued spending collections amid financial stress and liabilities.The agency also flagged promoter remuneration, alleging the directors drew a combined ₹24.92 crore in salaries from FY 2022-23 onwards.It said the Goel family held 86.31% shareholding, enabling approval of remuneration, and alleged Dinesh Kumar Goel drew about ₹56 lakh per month while Monila Goel received over ₹25 lakh monthly.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.body: Lucknow: PTC Industries Limited, a company manufacturing specialised metal components for defence, aerospace and other industries, has raised Rs 1,800 crore from Indian and international investors to expand its manufacturing capabilities and fund future growth.The Lucknow-based company announced on Tuesday that it had raised the money through a qualified institutions placement, a process through which listed companies sell shares to large institutional investors to raise funds.The company issued 8.54 lakh shares at Rs 21,060 each. Investor demand was more than five times the shares offered, indicating strong interest from domestic and foreign institutions.Among the major investors, Fidelity Investments contributed nearly Rs 850 crore, followed by Capital Group with Rs 355 crore and Fidelity International with Rs 150 crore. HDFC Mutual Fund, Tata AIA Life Insurance and other financial institutions also participated.The company said the funds would support expansion of existing facilities, development of new manufacturing projects, technological upgrades and possible acquisitions.PTC is expanding its advanced manufacturing facilities at the Lucknow node of the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor. Its subsidiary, Aerolloy Technologies, manufactures specialised titanium and high-performance metal products used in aircraft, defence equipment and other critical applications.PTC chairman and managing director Sachin Agarwal said the strong response from global investors reflected confidence in the company’s manufacturing capabilities and future growth plans.The company also operates through Trac Precision Solutions in the United Kingdom, strengthening its international manufacturing presence.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: KGMU designated as UP’s first centre of excellence in acute care precision medicine
articles.summary: KGMU named UP’s first acute care precision medicine centre, offering faster multiplex PCR diagnosis, affordable testing, pharmacogenomics and plans for next-gen sequencing.
articles.body: Lucknow: Patients in Uttar Pradesh are expected to get faster, more personalised and more affordable treatment after King George’s Medical University was nominated as the state’s first centre of excellence in precision medicine in acute care.Officials said the recognition is aimed at strengthening care for critically ill patients by enabling the university to expand advanced diagnostic and therapeutic services more quickly. Precision medicine, they said, focuses on tailoring treatment to an individual’s genetic profile, medical condition, test findings and response to drugs, instead of relying on a uniform approach.A major benefit highlighted by doctors is faster infection detection through multiplex PCR testing. The test can deliver key diagnostic results in around eight hours, compared with nearly 72 hours using conventional methods. Clinicians said this reduction in turnaround time can help doctors make treatment decisions earlier, which is crucial in intensive care settings.Cost was cited as another advantage. KGMU offers multiplex molecular screening for about Rs 2,000, while similar testing can cost around Rs 15,000 in private hospitals, making advanced diagnostics more accessible for a wider section of patients.The centre has also introduced pharmacogenomic testing to assess how a patient’s genes influence drug response. KGMU is also focusing on antimicrobial resistance by rapidly identifying infections and resistance markers, enabling more targeted antibiotic use.Prof Avinash Agrawal of the department of critical care medicine said the centre has carried out over 80,000 tests since 2023, including molecular diagnostics and pharmacogenomic investigations, and that the designation will further boost its capabilities.Vice-chancellor Prof Soniya Nityanand said the aim is to translate scientific advances into routine care and extend precision medicine to ordinary citizens.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Indian man travels across consulates for F1 visa interviews, gets visa after 13 rejections. In his 14th interview, he was asked to plan a 20-storey residential building
articles.summary: An Indian man claimed he finally got his F1 visa to study civil engineering in the US after being rejected 13 times at several consulates in India.
articles.body: An Indian man claimed he finally got his F1 visa to study civil engineering in the US after being rejected 13 times at several consulates in India. The man, identified as Prasanth, shared his derailed experience of rejections one by one and the questions the visa officers asked him in an NRI social media group. Once he got the same visa officer, and several visa officers refused to answer him why his visa application was getting denied. But he kept on booking for slots and in his last interview, he was even asked whether he was planning to commit some crime in the US -- he seemed so determined to go to the US. He said he was the last candidate on the day his application was accepted and all those present at the office at that time started clapping because the gruelling interview went on for around 50 minutes, he said.The first F-1 visa interview was in Mumbai where he was asked basic questions like why he wanted to study in the US etc. The second interview in Hyderabad was the same, with basic questions about course and university, followed by rejection. From the third interview onwards, the previous rejections started to concern the visa officers, as the third interviewer in Delhi asked him why his previous applications were rejected.Little did he know then that it was just the beginning. The 4th interview was again in Hyderabad. Rejected. The 5th interview was in Kolkata, where the visa officer asked him to apply for an Extraordinary Ability visa after knowing about his future business plans etc. The 6th and 7th were again in Hyderabad and were rejected. The 8th one was in Chennai -- rejected.In the 9th interview in Delhi, he was asked technical questions on civil engineering and about his past projects in India. He was even asked if he had to construct Burj Khalifa, how he would do that -- but rejection followed. It went on until his 14th attempt in Hyderabad. The visa officer went through his 13 rejections and appreciated his sincerity. During the interview, the visa officer asked to plan the construction of a 20-storey residential building with 5 apartments on each floor.The interview finally ended in success as the visa officer said she would approve his application. The man said he was the last candidate on that day and had to wait hours for the interview. Everyone at the office clapped after his application was approved, he said calling the day the 'golden day'.While many peopel congratulated him, many doubted the veracity of the story as they said it was almost impossible to get so many interview slots in India.You use AI every day. articles.title: SRFTI rusticates 6 students for assaulting VC, vandalising office
articles.summary: SRFTI Kolkata rusticates six students after alleged assault on VC Santosh Ajmera and vandalism of his office amid protests over campus clashes and CCTV plans.
articles.body: Kolkata: SRFTI on Thursday rusticated six students, one for assaulting vice-chancellor Santosh Ajmera, and the others for vandalising the VC’s chamber.The decision to expel the six – Shubham Waydande, Aaron P Joy, Appu Soman, Abhilash B Nair, Nachiket Shashikant Pawar and Dhivahar M – was recommended at an emergency meeting of the Dean Council that was attended by 11 faculty members, representatives of departments and the registrar.The council observed that such acts of physical violence pose a grave threat to campus safety, institutional discipline, dignity and security of the institute. It recommended that the VC take immediate measures to ensure safety on campus and ensure continuity of academic activities.Students have refused to attend classes since a clash erupted between them and Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat, an RSS affiliate, on Sept 26. The situation deteriorated further on Oct 4 after Bongiya Hindu Jagaran Manch staged a protest outside the institute and allegedly assaulted some students.On Thursday morning, when the VC reached his chamber, he found the window panes shattered and furniture covered in glass shards. He immediately met faculty members and ordered installation of CCTV cameras in the corridor outside his office, triggering another round of protest by the students. Later, when the VC was on his way to the guest house for lunch, he was heckled and assaulted.Ajmera, who took charge as VC about 15 days ago, in a statement condemned the attack on his office and person, calling it “completely unacceptable”. “The attack was cowardly, extremely disturbing and unfortunate. It was an act unbecoming of students belonging to an institute of repute like SRFTI. The actions of few students have disturbed peace, order and normal academic activities at the institute,” he said.Security officer Prabir Kumar Munshi said obstruction of staff members began two days ago when students started demonstrations inside the administration building. He claimed the staffers had to leave the building with police escort.“We are registering an FIR against Shubham Waydande, vice-president of the students’ union, for physically assaulting the VC. He was earlier involved in a case where four biometric machines were found damaged,” Munshi said. The Dean Council viewed the current incident of assault on the VC in conjunction with his earlier pending proceedings as a matter of serious concern for campus safety.“What is the difference between students and outsiders if both resort to physical violence when they disagree with a view or a person? I am now feeling insecure about going to the campus,” said a faculty member. A female faculty member complained to the VC that on Wednesday, some 20 students “kept opening” her office door while shouting slogans.The student union claimed the allegations were completely fabricated and a clear attempt by the VC to install CCTV on the campus. “The students of SRFTI have employed strictly non-violent and peaceful tactics during our protest. articles.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle gets snubbed in Greece too, no farewell planned for her; Greek leaders believe she's so brazen that she may force one send-off
articles.summary: Greek president Konstantinos Tasoulas has not planned any official farewell for Kimberly Guilfoyle as she leaves her ambassadorship amid turmoil.
articles.body: Greek president Konstantinos Tasoulas has not planned any official farewell for Kimberly Guilfoyle as she leaves her ambassadorship amid turmoil. According to protocol, a grand send-off is arranged when an ambassador ends their term but in this case, Guilfoyle is accused of many wrongdoings and her resignation was prompted by an undubious order from the White House that she had to resign. "Protocol has it that with every outgoing ambassador a courtesy call is placed with the head of state, the prime minister and the foreign minister," a source at the Athens embassy told the Daily Mail. "However, because of her sudden ousting she will not be allowed to say goodbye."A top aide for the Greek president, however, said that Guilfoyle is so brazen that she may forcefully extract a farewell from the Greek leadership. "She is so brazen that no one is discounting she might show up anyway to try to force a grand farewell despite her current ignominy," the aide told the Mail. "Anyone would be enormously embarrassed to do that, but this is Kimberly."Staffers at the US Embassy in Athens said her departure is "unprecedented.""We have never seen such a violent beheading of the mission. Usually, these push-outs happen quietly. This was abrupt," a staffer told the outlet."There is no semblance of shock, rather relief that she's been fired. She was horrible and mean and spoke down to just about everybody," another staffer said. "She simply wouldn't listen to anyone, even the most experienced career diplomats surrounding her."A Wall Street Journal report accused Guilfoyle of demanding $100,000 from MAGA donor Eric Deters in exchange for access with the Trump administration. Guilfoyle did not accept the allegations and said she will clear her name of it as she remains a supporter of President Trump. "Serving as the United States Ambassador to Greece has been the honor of a lifetime," she wrote. articles.title: Hillingdon Council urges residents to identify fly-tippers caught on CCTV as 300-plus fines total £134,000; England records 1.26 million incidents, with offenders facing £1,000 fines or five years in prison
articles.summary: Hillingdon Council in west London is urging residents to help identify people caught dumping rubbish illegally, posting CCTV images of suspected offenders
articles.body: Hillingdon Council in west London is urging residents to help identify people caught dumping rubbish illegally, posting CCTV images of suspected offenders on Facebook and Instagram as part of a wider crackdown on fly-tipping.The initiative involves sharing images of people allegedly leaving waste on streets and other public spaces, with the council appealing to residents for information that could help enforcement teams identify those responsible. It is believed to be the first time a council has launched such a public initiative to encourage residents to report the offence.Council says fly-tipping will not be toleratedA council spokesperson told The Telegraph that the authority was sending a clear message that illegal dumping would not be accepted in the borough.“We're sending a clear message that fly-tipping in our borough will not be tolerated. Fly-tipping is illegal, harms the environment and blights our neighbourhoods,” the spokesperson said.The council added that its social media posts reflected how seriously residents viewed the issue and said the approach had shown early signs of success.“Our social media posts prove just how important this issue is for our residents, and we're asking for their help to identify offenders. This practice has shown early success and we intend to continue in this manner,” the spokesperson added.The council posted images of three suspected offenders on Facebook this week, warning that people who dumped rubbish and drove away should not expect to escape consequences.“While most residents dispose of their waste responsibly, a small minority continue to think they can dump rubbish and drive away without consequences. They're wrong,” the authority said.Hillingdon steps up enforcement against illegal dumpingIn a recent incident, fly-tippers targeted St Anselm's Church car park, according to the council. The authority said those involved “weren't as anonymous as they thought” and appealed to the public for information to help enforcement teams identify them.The social media campaign forms part of a broader enforcement drive across Hillingdon. Council officers have already issued more than 300 fixed penalty notices, amounting to approximately £134,000.The authority has also carried out its first impounding and destruction of a vehicle linked to illegal waste dumping.Last year, a Ford Iveco flatbed truck was caught leaving waste on a residential road in Ickenham. The council's anti-social behaviour team used its CCTV network to locate the vehicle, which was subsequently seized in Hayes, impounded and crushed.“There’s no excuse for dumping waste illegally in Hillingdon when a range of free or low-cost disposal options are available,” the spokesperson said.The council said it would continue to pursue enforcement action where evidence allowed, including issuing fines, seizing and crushing vehicles, and pursuing prosecutions where possible.Fly-tipping offenders face fines and possible prison sentencesPeople caught fly-tipping can face fixed penalty notices of up to £1,000. More serious cases can be referred to magistrates' courts, where offenders may face unlimited fines or prison sentences of up to five years.Householders also have a legal responsibility to ensure that private waste-removal companies they hire hold a valid Environment Agency licence. They can face prosecution and fines if their waste is dumped illegally, including when they have paid a third party to remove it.Fly-tipping incidents rise across EnglandThe crackdown comes amid growing concerns about the scale and cost of illegal waste dumping. More than 1.26 million fly-tipping incidents were recorded last year, representing a 9 per cent increase on the previous year.The Government spent £19.3 million clearing large-scale fly-tipping incidents in England last year, nearly 50 per cent more than in the preceding 12 months.When the costs of clearing waste from private land and wider enforcement expenses are included, the total annual impact on the UK economy is estimated to exceed £390 million.You use AI every day. articles.title: Qatar painted sections of its roads blue to fight extreme heat; the 2019 pilot tested a coating designed to reflect 50% of sunlight
articles.summary: Public Works Authority Ashghal has completed a pilot of cool pavement on roads in Qatar. The authority announced the work on 19 August 2019.
articles.body: Public Works Authority Ashghal has completed a pilot of cool pavement on roads in Qatar. The authority announced the work on 19 August 2019. An asphalt-cooling material was applied to up to 200 metres of vehicle lanes on Abdullah bin Jassim Street, beside Souq Waqif, and to 200 metres of pedestrian and bicycle paths in front of Katara, the Cultural Village. According to an official from the Public Works Authority ('Ashghal') in Qatar, conventional asphalt absorbs up to 80 to 95% of sunlight, while the new coating reflects about 50%. Sensors will compare its temperature with conventional asphalt over an 18-month study, carried out with the Japanese company Oriental.Why is Qatar painting some roads blue instead of blackThe pilot used an asphalt-cooling material on parts of Abdullah bin Jassim Street, next to Souq Waqif. The authority says it was applied to vehicle lanes over a length of up to 200 metres. The same material was also tested on 200 metres of pedestrian and bicycle paths in front of Katara, the Cultural Village.The road was opened to traffic so that testing could begin. The authority says the aim is to measure how effective the material is and to judge whether the experiment succeeds. It adds that the result could lead to formal use of the material across the road network in the State of Qatar.How long will Qatar’s blue road study lastAshghal says the study will last 18 months. Based on the outcome, the authority will decide whether the pilot has succeeded and how widely the material could be applied. The announcement says road experts and contractors have installed special devices and sensors on the pilot sections.According to Ashghal, these sensors measure how well the material reduces asphalt temperature and compare the results with conventional asphalt. The authority says the work was carried out in cooperation with the Japanese company Oriental, which it describes as one of the leading companies in implementing this technology.Why does conventional asphalt absorb up to 95% of sunlightAshghal explains that conventional asphalt contributes to rising temperatures because it absorbs up to 80 to 95% of sunlight. Cool pavement, the authority says, reflects ultraviolet rays and absorbs less solar radiation. Ashghal adds that this can have a positive effect on overall temperature reduction, given the size of the areas covered by conventional asphalt.On the specification, Ashghal says cooled paving material can be made from traditional paving materials such as concrete. The authority says the new coating on the concrete asphalt layer reflects "about 50% of sunlight". It states that the coating consists of four layers: a primary layer, followed by three consecutive layers that reduce the heat absorbed from solar radiation.How does Qatar’s cool pavement improve road safetyThe announcement says a protective material has been applied to the ground markings. According to Ashghal, this shields the markings from contact with vehicles and increases their lifespan. The authority links cool pavement to energy efficiency and says research by environment and sustainability experts suggests it can reduce overall temperature and, as a result, emissions.Ashghal also cites research suggesting that cool paving material reduces heat-related illnesses and slows the formation of smog. The authority says it can improve pedestrians' ability to use the road and promote traffic safety, because light-coloured pavements reflect street lights and car headlights better and make vehicles more visible to drivers. In addition, Ashghal says that lowering air temperatures in residential areas can slow the chemical reactions in the atmosphere that cause smog.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: FSDA suspends railway’s base kitchen operations over lapses
articles.summary: UP FSDA suspends Lucknow railway base kitchen over hygiene and record lapses; cancels Saharanpur registration, seizes 978 kg in Kanpur, tests samples.
articles.body: Lucknow: The Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) found shortcomings in hygiene, food storage, staff cleanliness, drinking water testing, pest control and the maintenance of mandatory records during inspections of food catering units across the state, including 41 railway catering units and two units supplying food to airlines.The FSDA said operations at a base kitchen in Lucknow were suspended immediately, while the food registration of an establishment in Saharanpur was cancelled. Nearly one tonne of food items was seized in Kanpur Nagar.Teams inspected base kitchens and food storage premises associated with railway catering in Lucknow, Saharanpur, Kanpur Nagar, Agra, Chandauli, Gorakhpur, Ghaziabad, Moradabad, Varanasi, Bareilly and Jhansi. They found deficiencies related to cleanliness, drinking water testing reports, employees’ health certificates, pest control, stock registers and food-grade certificates for packaging materials at 30 units. Notices were issued to these units.At an establishment in Kanpur Nagar, the FSDA said it found 978 kg of a food item stored without a label or details of its manufacturing and use-by dates. The item was seized. Samples of 26 food items were also collected and sent to a laboratory for quality testing.Units supplying food to airlines at Lucknow and Varanasi airports were also inspected. An official said the inspections revealed several concerns, including some employees not wearing shoe covers and masks, the unavailability of required records and certificates, and labelling issues. articles.title: Formula 1 Heads to Austin
articles.summary: F1 Returns to America Formula 1 heads back to the United States next weekend for the United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas. Th...
articles.body:
Formula 1 heads back to the United States next weekend for the United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas. The October 23–25 race weekend marks the start of the championship's final stretch, with drivers and teams preparing for an important battle as the season moves toward its conclusion.

Circuit of the Americas is one of the most challenging tracks on the calendar, combining long straights, heavy braking zones and technical corners that test both driver skill and car performance. The 5.513-kilometer circuit features 20 turns, including the famous uphill run into Turn 1, where drivers often have opportunities to make daring overtakes.

Antonelli and Russell Lead the Championship Fight

Mercedes drivers Kimi Antonelli and George Russell have been among the major contenders throughout the 2026 season. Antonelli has collected victories at several circuits, including China, Japan and Italy, while Russell has delivered strong performances of his own, including wins in Azerbaijan and Austria.

Max Verstappen also remains an important contender after winning the Singapore and Bahrain Grands Prix. His ability to manage tire wear and capitalize on opportunities makes him a threat whenever Red Bull has a competitive car.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton will also be looking to challenge near the front. Both drivers have shown flashes of speed this season, and Austin could provide another opportunity for Ferrari to fight for a podium finish.

Tire management will be a major factor at Circuit of the Americas. The track's combination of high-speed corners and heavy braking can place significant demands on the tires, forcing teams to carefully balance outright pace with long-run performance.

Overtaking opportunities along the back straight could also make strategy especially important. Teams must decide when to pit, how to respond to safety cars and whether an alternative tire strategy could provide an advantage late in the race.

Qualifying will be important as well, but starting near the front does not guarantee success at a circuit where passing opportunities can develop throughout the field.

The United States Grand Prix is scheduled for Sunday, October 25, with the race beginning at 3 p.m. Central Time, or 4 p.m. Eastern.

With the championship battle continuing and several races remaining, Austin presents an important opportunity for the leading drivers to gain valuable points. Mercedes, Red Bull and Ferrari will all be looking to make their mark at one of Formula 1's most popular American venues.

The weekend promises another exciting chapter in the 2026 championship fight, with every position becoming increasingly valuable as the season approaches its final races.
